The Bakanh, or Pakanh, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the interior of the Cape York Peninsula in north Queensland. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Little is recorded of them beyond their name, their language and the rough bounds of their land, which lies between the Gulf coast and the central ranges. Their language belongs to the Paman branch of the Pama-Nyungan family. Neighbours on the map include the Wik, the Lama Lama and the Thaayorre. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
